bull.b: TSMC’s high advanced-node mix demonstrates strong positioning in the most technically demanding and valuable part of semiconductor manufacturing. Leadership across 2 nm, 3 nm, 5 nm and 7 nm supports customer relevance, pricing power and durable demand from high-performance computing and AI applications.

Exceptional margins and rising operating cash flow indicate substantial scale benefits, strong earnings quality and effective conversion of customer demand into financial resources. This cash generation supports technology investment, overseas expansion and shareholder distributions while the conservative balance sheet preserves financial flexibility.

The combination of unusually strong AI demand, a clear 2 nm expansion plan and an A14 production roadmap provides multi-year support for growth. TSMC is expanding capacity ahead of expected customer needs, reinforcing its role as a strategic manufacturing platform for advanced chip designers.

bear.b: TSMC’s growth model requires exceptionally high and sustained capital spending on fabs, equipment and packaging capacity. Although investment supports future revenue, weaker free-cash-flow conversion can reduce near-term financial flexibility and makes returns more sensitive to utilization, execution and semiconductor-cycle conditions.

The global manufacturing build-out and steep 2 nm ramp are expected to pressure gross margins even while revenue grows. New overseas facilities may initially operate below Taiwan’s scale and maturity, creating a durable profitability headwind that could moderate the benefit of leading-edge pricing and mix.

TSMC remains exposed to uneven semiconductor demand outside its strongest AI and high-performance-computing markets. Weakness in consumer and price-sensitive applications can increase revenue volatility, complicate capacity planning and leave the company more dependent on a narrower set of fast-growing end markets.
